content.text: An argument is **valid** when its conclusion must be true if all its premises are true. Validity says nothing about whether the premises are true.

content.definition: The pattern left when the content is replaced by letters, such as: If A then B. Not B. So not A.

content.text: A valid form stays valid whatever content fills it.

examples.title: Valid: modus tollens
lines: If you overslept, you are late.
examples.note: Form: If A then B. Not B. So not A. Every argument of this form is valid.

examples.title: Invalid: affirming the consequent
lines: If you overslept, you are late.
examples.note: Form: If A then B. B. So A. You could be late for another reason, such as traffic.

question.prompt: Which form is this? If A then B. Not B. So not A.
question.hint: Look at the second premise. Does it affirm A, or deny B?
question.explanation: Modus tollens denies the consequent: from If A then B and not B, it concludes not A. It is valid.
